sourceInformation.genre: Surgical action (arcade operation game) with a visual-novel story
sourceInformation.perspective: First-person surgeon’s-eye 3D operative field; staged third-person story scenes
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0, WebGPU with WebGL2 fallback, TSL ink filter, Rapier 0.19.3, Web Audio, Gamepad API, esbuild 0.28.2, AI Hub session client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Comic-book medical drama. Procedural toon geometry, ink outlines, manga tone, hand-painted organ textures made in code.
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, code-built keyframe clips, skinned strains, beat-driven organs and procedural follow-through
sourceInformation.audio: Original synthesized sequencer music, procedural effects, text-driven gibberish voices. Music 10%; effects and voices 80% by default.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, shared world, 1–4 players. Standalone couch co-op.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Node and Playwright: full bot/UI campaign, noisy input, 1–4 surgeon co-op, WebGPU/WebGL2/WebKit, synthesized audio, saves, dev tools, actual Hub harness, responsive screenshots. No FPS target.
sourceInformation.research: Supplied PLAN.md and its verified engine recipes; official AI Hub v1 protocol, released client and real conformance harness.

testingFeedback: 26 tracked issue groups fixed. Final suite: 94 checks. Viewport matrix: 19 clean screenshots.
8 classified critical: phase interlocks, exhausted clamps, armless attacks, moved anchors, excessive regrowth, shared suture tearing, invalid trophy geometry, and out-of-range skinning indices.
Most helpful: the end-to-end bot campaign, including one through four surgeons. It exposed cross-system blockers that isolated instrument checks missed.

Least helpful: PNG-size smoke checks; they only detect blank frames. Physical haptics and human audio quality: unknown. WebKit profiles are a stand-in for iOS Safari. Pad-only audio unlocking could not be proved in Chromium.
engineFeedback: Native toon materials, AnimationMixer, skinning and TSL let one procedural art style work on WebGPU and WebGL2.
Yes. Hairline geometry, torso winding, foreground occlusion, skinning bounds and ink-pass depth compositing needed visual verification.
The fixed-step surgical simulation: precise tool rules, beat clock, checkpoint data, bot and authoritative shared-world state.
Keeping animated portraits, multipass ink rendering and entity lifetimes correct across both graphics backends.
None. Three.js and Rapier are unmodified.
Make render-target UV orientation explicit and consistent across draw paths.
promptFeedback: The heartbeat pillar and concrete narrative beats gave mechanics, music and presentation one common purpose.
The minimum-vitals test conflicts with scripted arrests at 15. Ordinary danger and forced dramatic events need separate invariants.
Integrating the full tool/strain campaign, readable controller UI, procedural characters and authoritative co-op through one simulation.
Distinguish required behavior from optional visual flourishes, and specify the scripted-arrest test exceptions explicitly.

aiHub.name: Trauma Tempo: Encore
aiHub.tagline: Every heartbeat is a second chance.
aiHub.description: A rain-soaked medical drama where the heartbeat is the clock. Master eight instruments, confront seven musical parasites, and save St. Alder’s night shift alone or with a surgical team.
aiHub.controls: Right stick or mouse to aim, left stick or 1-8 for tools, R2 or left click to use
